label: shikimate degradation II
description: The MetaCyc shikimate degradation II pathway oxidizes shikimate with NAD+ to 3-dehydroshikimate and dehydrates it to protocatechuate in two reactions. This route is distinct from PQQ-dependent shikimate degradation I and the three-step quinate degradation II route. Strain R growth, uptake and gene-expression evidence is distinguished from ATCC 13032 QsuD and ATCC 13869 QsuB enzyme assays. Native database taxon associations do not establish shikimate uptake or growth in every strain.

mechanistic_edges.subject: MetaCyc:CPLX-7981
mechanistic_edges.description: QsuD catalyzes NAD-dependent shikimate oxidation. Native substrate Km is 46.6 mM. The curated complex comment reports NAD preference and >300-fold lower turnover with NADP; preference is not complete absence of NADP activity. The root chemistry audit verifies exact RXN-20484/RHEA:17742 molecular equivalence.

evidence.source_assertion: ENZRXN-17383 assigns CPLX-7981 to RXN-20484 with EV-EXP-IDA-PURIFIED-PROTEIN-HH and PMID18566515. Its separate PMID19376919 mutant evidence concerns strain R and is not merged into this purified ATCC 13032 claim.
RXN-20484 consumes shikimate and NAD, producing 3-dehydroshikimate, NADH and a proton. Its native direction is PHYSIOL-LEFT-TO-RIGHT and PWY-6419 is its named pathway.
The native shikimate Km entry is 46600 micromolar, citing PMID18566515. This value is a curated native annotation rather than a new measurement.
The native complex comment describes a homodimer, lower Km for quinate than shikimate, >3-fold greater catalytic efficiency for quinate, and >300-fold lower turnover with NADP than NAD.

mechanistic_edges.subject: RHEA:24849
mechanistic_edges.description: The terminal dehydration supplies protocatechuate to the explicitly linked downstream ortho-cleavage pathway. This interface does not add the downstream reactions as formal shikimate-II members or assert whole-route activity in every downstream-pathway organism.

evidence.source_assertion: PWY-6419 links its terminal protocatechuate product to PROTOCATECHUATE-ORTHO-CLEAVAGE-PWY. The pathway comment identifies protocatechuate as the two-step route endpoint and a substrate for downstream mineralization.
The downstream pathway begins with PROTOCATECHUATE-34-DIOXYGENASE-RXN consuming 3-4-DIHYDROXYBENZOATE; its common name is protocatechuate degradation II (ortho-cleavage pathway).

mechanistic_edges.subject: UniProtKB:A4QH18
mechanistic_edges.description: C. glutamicum R ShiA/cgR_2523 supports shikimate uptake for the pathway. Loss of shiA blocks shikimate growth and extracellular consumption; uptake increases in a shiA-expressing strain. QsuA/cgR_0492 is a distinct gene. Primary abstract scope does not establish proton coupling or transport stoichiometry.

mechanistic_edges.subject: UniProtKB:A4QH19
mechanistic_edges.description: R-strain ShiR/cgR_2524 increases shiA transcription in shikimate-containing cultures; disrupting shiR reduces induction. This is gene-expression control. The inspected primary abstract does not establish direct shikimate binding to ShiR or the construct used for the separately annotated promoter-binding assay.
